notes:
Simulator test harness, plus a UI bug it found immediately. THE HARNESS closes the gap that slowed every playback investigation this week: the speakers were fully visible over SOAP and the app was not, so 'the app shows X but the speaker is doing Y' always needed Tom to look at his phone. Running Sorriva in the iOS Simulator puts its log, database and process on this Mac. tools/sonos.py — discovery, transport, queue, registered shares, volume, and testing(), which enforces the nominated zone list, mutes, and restores prior state even if the body throws. tools/sim.py — locates the app container by metadata rather than a remembered UUID (it changed mid-session), reads the database READ-ONLY so it can never corrupt a running app, reads the log, snapshots container AND device keychain (the keychain is device-level, so a container-only copy silently loses the NAS credentials). tools/check.py — speakers and app side by side, with snapshot/restore. Verified end to end: a track read from the app's own library, queued per the playback contract, confirmed PLAYING on a real speaker with a real duration, then restored — at volume zero throughout.

GUARDRAILS ARE ENCODED, NOT REMEMBERED. tools/test-zones.json names the three zones Tom nominated and mutes during tests; his reasoning is quoted there — silence makes the hour irrelevant, so there are no quiet hours. It also records that UI taps can start real playback and no code can intercept that, so the list governs behaviour and not just scripts. Zones absent from the list are refused.

FOUND BY THE HARNESS, FIXED: the scan confirmation alert was raised 0.4s after the action sheet closed and hoped the sheet had gone. When it hadn't, SwiftUI silently dropped the alert and the tap did nothing — the queued scan then sat unnoticed until onAppear happened to raise it on a later visit. Now raised from the sheet's onDismiss, which is the actual signal.

ALSO FOUND, LOGGED, NOT FIXED: SMBClient slices 64 bytes off a response buffer without checking it has 64 bytes (bSMBClientByteReaderOutOfBounds) — a hard crash, not simulator-specific, that on device would look like the app vanishing mid-scan. Our own timeout-driven NWConnection.cancel() is the plausible trigger. It presents as a HANG rather than a crash because lldb holds the process: kill -9 fails and simctl shutdown never completes.

Test library seeded in the simulator: 95 tracks, 8 albums, artwork on all 8, resumed cleanly after the crash — which also proved the scan ledger's resume works across a hard failure.
